knowledge:
- key_parameters: chosenGenome=The BSgenome package or DNAString representing the reference genome ;; firstCutter=The recognition sequence of the primary restriction enzyme (e.g., "aagctt") ;; secondCutter=The recognition sequence of the secondary restriction enzyme (e.g., "catg") ;; readLength=The length of the sequenced reads in base pairs ;; useOnlyIndex=Logical; set to TRUE if using a BAM file without "chr" prefixes to match the virtual fragment library naming style ;; viewpointChromosome=The chromosome containing the 4C-seq viewpoint ;; viewpointInterval=A vector of start and end coordinates defining the viewpoint region ;; regionCoordinates=A vector of start and end coordinates defining the near-cis region to select for visualization ;; distanceFromVP=The genomic distance from the viewpoint used to calculate quality control read distribution statistics
- alternatives: BWA is recommended for initial read alignment due to speed and mismatch control; SAMtools and BEDtools are recommended for pre-filtering BAM files; RCircos is used as an alternative for plotting inter-chromosomal (trans) interactions; statistical enrichment methods (e.g., spider plots) are preferred for far-cis and trans interaction analysis
- when_to_use: Use this package when analyzing 4C-seq data to identify and visualize genomic regions interacting with a specific viewpoint, particularly for near-cis regions
- pitfalls: Blind fragments can introduce significant bias and should generally be excluded (they are filtered out by default); self-ligation can cause extreme read counts immediately adjacent to the viewpoint, so these adjacent fragments should be removed during near-cis selection; ensure that chromosome naming conventions ("chr1" vs "1") are consistent between the BAM file and the virtual fragment library to avoid mapping failures

workflows.name: standard_4cseq_analysis
workflows.intent: Perform a complete 4C-seq analysis workflow from virtual fragment library creation and read mapping to normalization, quality control, and near-cis visualization.
input: fetalLiverVP.bed (BED file containing points of interest and viewpoint coordinates)
BSgenome.Mmusculus.UCSC.mm9 (installed BSgenome package for the reference genome)
workflows.stages: 1. Create a virtual fragment library for the restriction enzymes and genome ;; 2. Load aligned reads and points of interest ;; 3. Initialize the Data4Cseq object ;; 4. Map reads to the virtual fragment library ;; 5. Select near-cis fragments around the viewpoint ;; 6. Normalize fragment read counts (RPM) ;; 7. Perform quality control on read distribution ;; 8. Visualize near-cis interactions using coverage plots and heatmaps
workflows.code:
library(BSgenome.Mmusculus.UCSC.mm9)
createVirtualFragmentLibrary(chosenGenome = Mmusculus, firstCutter = "aagctt", secondCutter = "catg", readLength = 54,  libraryName = "myFullFetalLiverVFL.csv")

library(GenomicAlignments)
libraryFile <- system.file("extdata", "vfl_aagctt_catg_mm9_54_vp.csv", package="Basic4Cseq")
bamFile <- system.file("extdata", "fetalLiverShort.bam", package="Basic4Cseq")
liverReads <- readGAlignments(bamFile)

pointsOfInterestFile <- system.file("extdata", "fetalLiverVP.bed", package="Basic4Cseq")
liverPoints<-readPointsOfInterestFile(pointsOfInterestFile)

liverData = Data4Cseq(viewpointChromosome = "10", viewpointInterval = c(20879870, 20882209), readLength = 54, pointsOfInterest = liverPoints, rawReads = liverReads)

rawFragments(liverData)<-readsToFragments(liverData, libraryFile)

nearCisFragments(liverData)<-chooseNearCisFragments(liverData, regionCoordinates = c(20800000, 21100000))

library("caTools")
nearCisFragments(liverData)<-normalizeFragmentData(liverData)

getReadDistribution(liverData, useFragEnds = TRUE, outputName = "")

visualizeViewpoint(liverData, plotFileName = "", mainColour = "blue", plotTitle = "Fetal Liver Near-Cis Plot", loessSpan = 0.1, maxY = 6000, xAxisIntervalLength = 50000, yAxisIntervalLength = 1000)

drawHeatmap(liverData, plotFileName = "", xAxisIntervalLength = 50000, bands = 5)
